subject: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Hi team,

Quick summary: during a paid demo for BrightChat this morning Olivia saw what looked like the SDK client issuing rapid retries on a 503 then subsequently sending duplicate generation requests back-to-back. The result was higher token usage than expected and two partial responses in the UI. Customer was concerned about cost and hallucination surface area.

What I have attached: brightchat_session_20260310.log (server request/response traces), sdk_client_trace.zip (client side debug logs), and a short screenshare recording. Repro steps are terse in the logs but look like: 1) intermittent 503 from hosted runtime under burst, 2) SDK retry kicks in, 3) the client replays the request while KV-cache not primed, 4) runtime returns partial tokens twice.

Ask: can runtime/serving confirm whether our retry/backoff client behavior can lead to duplicate generation tokens when combined with autoscaling-driven 503s? If it's a configuration mismatch (client retries too aggressively vs server idempotency), we need a mitigation for the customer ASAP and a product ask to make the SDK/Runtime interplay clearer in docs or add a server-side duplicate-detection knob.

Customer impact: production trial starting next week. Olivia is worried about token burn and unexpected output.

Next steps I'd like:
- Dev: quick triage to see if we can reproduce locally or point to a code path in the runtime.
- Hiro: if this is runtime behavior, help prioritize a short-term mitigation and a longer-term product change.
- Evelyn: help craft a response and suggested configuration/workaround for BrightChat.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(Attachment: brightchat_session_20260310.log, sdk_client_trace.zip, screenshare_demo_03-10.mp4)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Thanks Marissa, attaching a couple quick observations after an initial grep of the logs. I extracted the client timestamps and server request ids. It looks like the SDK issues an exponential-backoff retry after 503 with no idempotency token set, so the runtime sees two different request_ids for effectively the same user prompt within ~1.2s. Server returned HTTP 200 twice with different partial-token allocations.

Preliminary notes:
- The client retry window is short (initial backoff 200ms, jitter disabled in this build).
- The runtime currently treats each request as unique unless an idempotency-key header is present.
- Autoscaler in hosted path sometimes returns 503 during cold-starts; the SDK retry combined with missing idempotency leads to duplicate generation runs.

I can try to repro in staging with a simulated 503 window. If we confirm, short-term mitigation could be: enable jitter + increase initial backoff in the SDK and recommend setting an idempotency header from the client. Longer-term: runtime could accept a client idempotency token and dedupe across a small time window.

I'll spin up a local scenario and ping once I have a repro.

-Dev
(Attachment: extracted_request_ids.txt)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Thanks for the quick look, Dev.

Couple of clarifications from runtime side:
- We do not currently dedupe generation requests by default because idempotency detection for streaming/generative responses is non-trivial (partial tokens and KV cache state).
- There is an internal flag that can cause the serving layer to check an idempotency header and short-circuit duplicates for N seconds; it's not exposed to customers in hosted mode.
- Autoscaler 503s during cold-start are expected occasionally; however observed behavior (complete second generation returned) suggests the first 503 might have been a stale 503 while the request still reached a warm backend due to load-balancer retries. Need the full traces to understand the exact path.

Short-term proposal (priority: P1 for this customer trial):
1) Expose a recommended SDK config: enable jitter, initial_backoff 500ms, max_retries 2, and strongly recommend setting X-Idempotency-Key for user-originated completions.
2) Ops can enable the internal dedupe flag for BrightChat account on hosted for the trial window — requires approval from product/security.
3) Product: track an onboarding item to add official runtime support for idempotency tokens with clear behavior for streaming responses.

Marissa — can you confirm whether BrightChat can set an idempotency key from their desktop/web client? If not, we should push the ops-side temporary flag.

Hiro
Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@brightchat.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Olivia,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. I'm forwarding our internal triage — the short version: we see the SDK retry + a short 503 window leading to duplicate generation runs. Dev is reproducing in staging and Hiro has proposed an immediate mitigation (ops enable dedupe flag) and a recommended SDK config change (increase backoff, enable jitter, track idempotency key).

Can you confirm whether your client can send an idempotency token for the user prompt (a UUID per user interaction)? If you can't, we'll request a temporary ops-side change for your account while we implement a formal runtime feature.

We want to avoid any unexpected token usage during your trial. We'll share a mitigations plan today.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@brightchat.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: support@brightchat.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Marissa, team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We can add an idempotency UUID on the web client for each compose event; engineering will need a short spec. For the short-term trial we would appreciate the ops-side dedupe flag while our change ships (expected in 4 business days). Cost sensitivity is the main driver here.

Please let me know the exact header name you prefer and any constraints (TTL, max length).

— Olivia
Head of Integrations | BrightChat

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK retry/backoff anomaly observed in BrightChat demo - needs runtime input

Follow-up after product sync:

Decisions & action items (owner -> ETA):
- Ops (SRE): enable internal-dedupe flag for BrightChat account for a 7-day trial window. (Assigned to oncall; ETA: 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC)
- SDK team: publish temporary recommended config snippet and patch v0.9.7 to set default jitter and initial_backoff to 500ms; include an example for X-Idempotency-Key. (Owner: Dev Patel; ETA: 2026-03-16)
- Runtime/Product: scope formal idempotency support for streaming completions with documented behavior and retention window. (Owner: Hiro Tanaka/Product; ETA: 2026-04-20)
- Customer comms: Marissa & Evelyn to send an email acknowledging mitigations and next steps once ops confirms flag. (ETA: 2026-03-12 end of day)

I filed INF-7892 to track the runtime feature. Marissa, please hold off on public-facing guidance until ops confirms the flag is active.

Camila Reyes
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
